clue.text: Drug dealer quick to conceal wrongdoing

indicators.note: one word hides another inside it, so the word for quick wraps round the wrongdoing

parts.note: pacy means fast-moving
harm as an injury or wrong done

explanation.surface: A drug pusher who is swift to cover up a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug dealer' suggests a criminal, but the definition is a perfectly legal shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's shop dispenses and sells medicines, so it is literally a dealer in drugs.

clue.text: Parents accepting not one artist will create landscape

indicators.note: the two parents take the other words in between them

parts.note: pa and ma
no means not any, not one
RA, a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Mum and dad, with no painter, will produce a scenic view.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide unbroken view of a landscape or scene.

clue.text: A dozen letters on large bunch of keys

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: the first twelve letters of the alphabet run A to L

explanation.surface: Twelve letters on a large keyring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keys' are low islands or reefs, as in the Florida Keys, not things that open locks.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring of coral reefs and islets, a cluster of keys or cays.

clue.text: Complain about noise made by drunkard in Barnet

definitions.note: barnet means hair, here a hairstyle in particular

indicators.note: the word for complain wraps round the noise

parts.note: moan means to grumble
hic is a hiccup, the drunk's comic noise

explanation.surface: A drunk in a north London suburb is griping about the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but in rhyming slang Barnet Fair means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican is a hairstyle with a central strip of upright hair and shaved sides.

clue.text: Baby animal number five or eight, perhaps

parts.note: a cub is a young fox, bear or lion
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A young animal with a number, perhaps five or eight.
explanation.walkthrough: Eight is two times two times two, so it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight equals two raised to the third power, making it a perfect cube.

clue.text: Sound of strike catching a six-footer, a pugilist

indicators.note: the sound of the blow holds the insect inside it, as a hand catches something

parts.note: bam is the noise of a blow landing
an insect has six legs, so an ant is a six-footer

explanation.surface: A noisy punch lands on a very tall boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall man; it is an insect, with six feet. Bantamweight is a light boxing class, and the boxer is called a bantam.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a boxer in the bantamweight division, one of the lighter weight classes.

clue.text: Ace assistant keeping control in general

indicators.note: the ace and the assistant hold the control word inside them

parts.note: PA, a personal assistant
a grip on something is control of it

explanation.surface: A top aide keeps a firm grip on the commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcus Agrippa was the Roman general behind Augustus's victory at Actium.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrippa was a celebrated Roman military commander, Augustus's right-hand man.

clue.text: Great Dane barking where refreshments are served

indicators.note: barking means mad in British slang, so the letters go wild

parts.note: the dog breed's letters are the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A big dog barks at the place where snacks are on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' fits the dog, but it is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor café serving tea and light refreshments.

clue.text: Playing match with nothing in it, Real's great scorer

indicators.note: playing around with the letters reorders them
the word is emptied, leaving just its outer letters

parts.note: only its outside letters are used
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer at Real Madrid is a great goalscorer in an empty-netted match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' suggests a footballer at Real Madrid; it is a writer of musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler was a great composer, someone who writes orchestral scores.

clue.text: Hating the novel of one odd writer about quiet house

indicators.note: the pen and the reordered word go round the quiet house, holding it inside
the letters of one are made odd, put into a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written
a Bic is a well-known brand of ballpoint pen
p is piano, the musical instruction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the book written by an eccentric author about a silent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The novel' looks like a book, but here it means anything new.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophobia is fear or dislike of new things, so a neophobic person shuns novelty.

clue.text: Dramatic heroine leaves for a meal with princess

parts.note: cress is a salad leaf
Princess Ida is a Gilbert and Sullivan heroine

explanation.surface: A leading lady leaves to dine with a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, but it is salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cressida is the faithless heroine of Shakespeare's play Troilus and Cressida.

clue.text: Contact teacher's ending with a head

indicators.note: the possessive teacher's ending means its final letter only

parts.note: only its last letter is taken
each means per head, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with a headmaster after the teacher's finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach someone is to get in touch with them, as by phone or letter.

clue.text: Old widow's on line computer lessons

parts.note: re means on the subject of
ICT, information and communication technology, is the British school subject

explanation.surface: An elderly widow is taking computer classes online.
explanation.walkthrough: ICT is the name of the computing subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Relict is an archaic word for a widow, the one left behind after a spouse's death.

clue.text: Model worker not meeting deadlines

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
work that misses its deadline is late

explanation.surface: An exemplary employee who never meets a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model worker' reads as a paragon; the definition is the noun 'model', a pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or model from which copies are made.

clue.text: Almost grasping wine vessel filled with claret

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: venal means mercenary, open to bribery
cava is Spanish sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Nearly reaching for a vessel full of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is slang for blood, so the vessel is a vein, not a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: The vena cava is the large vein returning blood to the heart; claret is old slang for blood.

clue.text: Fail to get breaks once in Cambridge University also

indicators.note: the archaic word for breaks goes inside the university's initials

parts.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts
sunders is an old-fashioned word for breaks apart, hence once
and adds something, like also

explanation.surface: Someone fails to grasp the holidays at Cambridge, too.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge University points to England, but the university is MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: To misunderstand is to fail to grasp the meaning of something.

clue.text: Freud probably spent this second relaxing

parts.note: chilling is slang for taking it easy

explanation.surface: Freud likely spent a moment unwinding.
explanation.walkthrough: Freud lived in Vienna, so his money was in Austrian currency, used before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The schilling was Austria's currency, which a Viennese like Freud would have paid with.

clue.text: Kind of drink I really drink

parts.note: taken as written
so as in I so want that
tonic water, a mixer

explanation.surface: Someone's describing the type of beverage they truly drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotonic sports drinks have the same salt concentration as body fluids.

clue.text: Hunting game, pass around live badgers

indicators.note: the word for pass goes round the word for live

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it over
are as in to exist, they are
to badger and to hound both mean to pester

explanation.surface: Animals in a hunt chase round lively badgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badgers' reads as the animals, but it is the verb meaning pesters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hare and hounds is a paper-chase game in which runners pursue a leader laying a trail.

clue.text: Two chessmen sharing a square is cheating

indicators.note: the two pieces overlap so that one letter does double duty

parts.note: a rook and a king

explanation.surface: Two chess pieces on the same square is against the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of one piece is also the first of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle them, so rooking is cheating or fleecing.

clue.text: Transport locum doctor around during uprising

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read from the bottom up
the two words go round the word for during

parts.note: a locum is a stand-in, a sub
MO, medical officer
in as in in the night

explanation.surface: Taking a stand-in doctor round during a rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is the full old name for a bus, a form of public transport.

clue.text: Reason against blocking tidal flow up in channel

indicators.note: the argument word sits inside, blocking the flow
in a down answer the word reads upwards

parts.note: ebb, the receding tide
the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: An argument against damming the tide in a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests water; it is a TV channel, the BBC's main one.
explanation.definitionFit: BBC One is the flagship television channel of the British Broadcasting Corporation.

clue.text: Dog turning right in grand residence

indicators.note: the short word for the dog is turned round

parts.note: lab is short for labrador
moral means right in the ethical sense

explanation.surface: A dog is turning right inside a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: BALMORAL is the royal family's castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle is the monarch's grand Scottish estate home.

clue.text: Hip black plates the ultimate in book printing method

indicators.note: to plate is to coat or cover, so the two words wrap round the letter

parts.note: in means fashionable
jet is a deep black

indicators.note: only the last letter of book is wanted

parts.note: its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Trendy black illustrations crown a book's print technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkjet printers spray tiny droplets of ink onto paper, a common printing technique.

clue.text: Tipped over fruit juice drink in drinking bowl

indicators.note: tipped over means turned upside down, so the letters read the other way

parts.note: OJ, orange juice
rum, the spirit

explanation.surface: Juice and liquor spilled into a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A jorum is a large drinking vessel or bowl, also its contents, often punch.

clue.text: Girl from Spain, and something she inherits

parts.note: E is Spain's international vehicle registration letter
DNA is the genetic material passed from parents

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl and her inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a female first name, so it fits a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Old guy, one horny bounder from Africa

parts.note: to guy someone is to tease or rib them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ageing lecherous cad who has come over from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny bounder' suggests a lustful rogue; it is a leaping animal with horns. Guy as a verb means to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope, horned and a springy leaper.

clue.text: Partridge cages keep out a big star?

indicators.note: the first name surrounds the words for keep out, as a cage holds a bird

parts.note: Alan Partridge is Steve Coogan's comic character, a British TV presenter
to debar is to exclude

explanation.surface: A partridge in a cage keeps a famous celebrity away.
explanation.walkthrough: Partridge looks like the bird; it is Alan Partridge, the comedy character of British TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is a red giant, the brightest star in Taurus; the question mark plays on star as celebrity.

clue.text: Flipping blue gag nearly holds interest

indicators.note: the letters run backwards, flipped over
the phrase contains the answer within its letters

parts.note: the run of letters across these words, read backwards, gives the answer

explanation.surface: A crude joke, flipping close to the line, still grabs the attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild expletive; it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone is to occupy or hold their attention and interest.

clue.text: Mike goes after kind of wood yielding resin

indicators.note: Mike is placed following the timber, so it comes second

parts.note: balsa is a very light timber
mic is short for microphone, also spelt mike

explanation.surface: Mike follows a type of timber that produces sap.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is an aromatic resin, so anything balsamic gives or contains balsam.
